Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Absolutive (NOM for S, ACC for non-human O) is zero-marked.
curated_comment: Dharumbal (dhar1248, ISO xgm, Pama-Nyungan, Queensland) is a consistently ergative language per Terrill (2002). ERG suffix -ru/-ngu/-u/-Cu marks all transitive subjects regardless of tense, mood, animacy, agentivity, or clause type. GB409_6-7 (aspect) and GB409_12-13 (realis/irrealis) are marked '?' because these grammatical categories do not exist in Dharumbal: the verbal system distinguishes Non-Past, Past, Far-Past, Imperative, Purposive, but not perfective/imperfective or realis/irrealis. GB409_16-17 resolved to 1 (no topicality split documented; consistent ergative). GB409_22 corrected to 0: the 'unknown conditioning' in the source (Terrill §4.1.3) refers to the overt accusative marker on human O, not to conditioning of ERG marking on A. ERG=INST syncretism confirmed (GB409_24=1). Glottocode dhar1248 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: All three persons have distinct ERG pronoun forms: 1sg ngatha, 2sg nginda, 3sg nhula (Terrill §4.2).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Distinct ERG pronoun forms for all persons.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: Distinct ERG pronoun forms for all persons.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs take ERG suffix -ru/-ngu/-u/-Cu; example (4) p.30.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Perfective/imperfective aspect is not a morphological category in Dharumbal; tense categories are Non-Past, Past, Far-Past (Terrill §5.1).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Perfective/imperfective aspect is not a morphological category in Dharumbal.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Past tense examples (ex.53-57) show ERG on transitive subjects consistently.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Non-past examples (ex.49-52) show ERG on transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: All main clause declaratives show ERG; example (15) p.31.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Imperative and purposive clauses also show ERG on transitive subjects (ex.18, 27, 80).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Realis/irrealis is not a morphological category in Dharumbal; tense/mood system has no such distinction.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Realis/irrealis is not a morphological category in Dharumbal.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Agentive A takes ERG; example (4) p.30.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Non-agentive A (e.g., caused events) also takes ERG; causative constructions (§5.2.1) show ERG on causer regardless of volitional control.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality conditioning of ergative marking described or evidenced anywhere in Terrill (2002); consistent ERG system applies to topical A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No topicality conditioning; consistent ERG system applies to non-topical A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate A consistently takes ERG; example (4) p.30.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No animacy split in ERG marking documented; no evidence of inanimate A behaving differently.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Main clauses consistently show ERG; example (4) p.30.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Subordinate purposive clauses show ERG on transitive subjects (§6.4.2, ex.114-116).

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: The 'unknown conditioning' in Terrill §4.1.3 refers to the overt accusative marker -(n)a on human O (object), not to any conditioning of ERG marking on A. The ERG suffix itself is regular and conditioned only by phonology.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Possessive = -ngunh (Terrill §4.1.8); entirely distinct from ERG suffix. No ERG=GEN syncretism.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The case chapter heading names the merged case 'Ergative/Instrumental' (§4.1.1, p.30). Single suffix marks both transitive subject and instrument.
